title: Runtime Security Analysis of Monolithic 3D Embedded DRAM with Oxide-Channel Transistor
problem: Monolithic 3D eDRAM with oxide-channel transistors is vulnerable to Rowhammer/Rowpress attacks and M3D-specific electrical disturbances that degrade data integrity and security.
motivation: 3D integration increases memory density but introduces vertical coupling and new attack vectors; security implications for M3D eDRAM must be understood before widespread deployment.
method: Characterizes Rowhammer/Rowpress vulnerabilities in IWO eDRAM across 2D and M3D configurations; examines electrical disturbances from memory-on-logic and memory-on-memory stacking; evaluates physical design and architecture mitigation strategies.
key_novelty: First comprehensive security and disturbance analysis of M3D eDRAM with oxide-channel transistors identifying M3D-specific vulnerability vectors.
contributions: First security analysis of IWO eDRAM in monolithic 3D integration
Identifies 300nm minimum vertical interlayer distance to mitigate disturbances in memory-on-memory stacking
Characterizes read bitline crosstalk sensitivity to high-speed logic switching
Demonstrates 30× resilience improvement over SOTA memory access transistors against Rowhammer
limitations: Not discussed; study is primarily characterization-based.
primary_theme: Security of 3D embedded DRAM with oxide transistors
